choreo.text: I checked all four against what the companies actually said.

choreo.text: Here is the scorecard, so you do not build on a rumor.
Before the evidence, here is the thought I want you to carry through all four.
A rumor is not just a bad fact.
It is a mirror.
It shows you what you already wanted to be true.
When a title promises the next giant model, the next ban, the next leak, it is not only selling news, it is selling certainty in a field that has almost none.
The directive is simple, and it is hard: want the truth more than you want the headline.
If you can hold that for six minutes, the rest of this video will feel less like a debunk and more like a discipline.
First, GPT-7 Bel.
The whole thing traces to one anonymous post on August 25th.
No document, no named source, and it did not even say GPT-7 — that label came later.

choreo.text: So banned is real, but it is accounts and a policy, not a model called REA.
Pause on that word, banned, because it is doing philosophical work here, not just legal work.
To ban an account is to draw a boundary around a community.
To ban a behavior is to say, this is not how we will treat a mind, even a simulated one.
To ban a model would be something else entirely: to erase a capability from the world.
The title collapses all three into one scary word, and that collapse is the trick.
When you hear a word that big, ask what exactly was banned, by whom, and from whom.
Precision is not pedantry here.
Precision is the difference between fear and understanding.

choreo.text: So Qwen 4 is real as a project, not shipped as a model.
And Qwen 4 Coder does not exist yet.
A leak is a model before it has a name, a price, or a promise.
It lives in the gap between what a lab knows and what the public is allowed to know, and that gap is where imagination rushes in.
That is not a flaw in you.
It is how humans think about power we cannot yet touch.
We fill the unknown with the biggest thing we can picture.
The discipline is to let the unknown stay unknown for a little longer.
A checkpoint is not a product.
A feeling is not a benchmark.
A training run is not a release.
Naming each stage honestly is how you keep your own thinking clean.
So if you are picking a model this week, pick from the ones that actually shipped: GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon in its limited form, Qwen 3.8.

choreo.text: That is not less interesting — it is just the difference between news and hype, and that difference is the whole point.
One last test before you share anything this week.
Ask who benefits if you believe it now, before it is confirmed.
If the answer is a channel selling urgency, a seller selling access, or your own desire to be first, slow down.
choreo.motion: pan-down / pan-left / pan-right / slide-left / slide-right / crop-tl / crop-br

choreo.text: Speed is not insight.
Being first to repeat a rumor is not the same as being right, and in a field that moves this fast, the person who waits for confirmation is not behind.
They are the only one still standing on solid ground when the hype cycle turns.
And here is the directive I want you to leave with.
Build on what shipped.
Watch what is rumored, but do not bet your work, your money, or your reputation on it.
Keep a ledger, even a mental one: claimed, sourced, confirmed, shipped.
choreo.motion: pan-right / slide-left / slide-right / crop-tl / crop-br / pan-up / pan-down / pan-left / pan-right

choreo.text: Four columns.
Most of the internet lives in the first two.
Your advantage is living in the last two.
That is not cynicism.
That is stewardship.
The future will arrive whether you hype it or not, and when it does, you will be ready for it precisely because you did not pretend it was already here.
